description: Check a landlord's rent-increase notice for a private residential tenancy in Scotland, outside a rent control area: whether it gives at least three months' notice, whether the rent has already gone up in the 12 months before, and whether it is on the prescribed form; when the new rent can start, and the last day to refer it to a rent officer. Scotland only; it does not judge whether the new rent is fair.

history.description: Whether the rent has gone up before: none, increased (give lastIncrease), or unknown.

lastIncrease.description: If the rent went up before, the day that increase took effect, as YYYY-MM-DD. If a rent officer or the tribunal set it, the day the landlord’s notice would have taken effect.

prescribedForm.description: Whether the notice is on the prescribed rent-increase notice form.

received.description: The day the tenant received the notice, as YYYY-MM-DD.

starts.description: The day the notice says the new rent starts, as YYYY-MM-DD.

name: check_scottish_rent_increase_notice
title: Scottish rent increase check
